literal: If a drop of the sky falls except, then, right there, green grass's tip to see is rare.
translation: Unless drops of rain fall from the sky, it is impossible to see even the tip of a single blade of green grass.
modern: வானத்திலிருந்து மழைத்துளி விழுந்தால் ஒழிய, அந்த இடத்திலே ஒரு பச்சைப் புல்லின் நுனியைக் கூடக் காண்பது அரிதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of rain for terrestrial life by focusing on its simplest form: grass. The poet states that without rain falling from the sky (விசும்பின் துளி), one cannot even see the tip (தலை) of a blade of green grass (பசும்புல்). The word 'தலை' (literally 'head') is used here to denote the very first shoot or tip of the grass that emerges from the soil. By showing that even the humblest and most resilient plant cannot sprout without rain, the couplet emphasizes that all life on earth is entirely dependent on water from above.
